To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Information Literacy 2.o is a more holistic and more critical view on Information literacy that is based on the assumption that the users of information systems are co-producers of information.
Information Literacy is a dynamic concept and that the library-based view has to be complemented by an Information Literacy 2,0 view.

the library-based view on IL, for which the Melvil Dewey stands in the title, has to be complemented by a more holistic, critical view on IL, with an emphasis on learning by doing (John Dewey), and on promoting reflection on the production of information and knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the Information Literacy of students in Germany is changing.
the question: How does Information Literacy 2.o differ from traditional Information Literacy?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Information Literacy 1.0 is still needed, but Information Literacy 2.o is also needed.
Information Literacy has to be understood as a process of lifelong learning and that it should be seen as a holistic concept, which has to be integrated in a more holistic concept of learning.
the library-based view on IL is still valid and necessary, but has to be extended by the more holistic and critical approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Information Literacy 2.o is not a replacement for the library-based view but a supplement.
Information Literacy 2.o is not only a matter of information and information technology.
Information Literacy 2.o should be a "critical Information Literacy" which is based on the user's own experiences with information and which is not only library based.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Information Literacy 2.o should be a central part of any Information Literacy program.
the library-based view has to be complemented by the more holistic one.
Information Literacy 2,0 is a necessary supplement to the library-based view of Information Literacy.
